story.title: Why this exists
story.p1: Every board comes with its own app, its own login and its own logbook. Climb a Kilter at your gym and a MoonBoard on holiday and you have two histories that never meet.
story.p2: Then one of those apps vanished overnight and climbers lost their logbooks with it. That is what happens when one company owns the only way into hardware you already paid for.
story.link: What happened, and how to get your data out

who.title: Who builds it
who.body: It started in 2024 with one climber and a repo, and it is still the kind of project people work on in the evenings. Bugs get found by someone standing at the wall, not by a QA team.

next.title: What's next
next.body: More boards, better offline, and getting your data out as easily as it went in. The roadmap is public and the arguments about it happen on Discord.

why.title: Why this page exists
why.p1: Boardsesh is free and open source, and it always will be. Running it costs real money: hosting, the database, and infrastructure bills add up as more climbers join.
why.p2: We promise not to enshittify Boardsesh, and self-hosting will always be an option. If you get something out of it and can spare it, chipping in keeps the lights on.

intro.title: Legal & Intellectual Property Policy
intro.p1: Boardsesh is a free, open-source, community-built alternative for browsing and interacting with standardised LED climbing training boards (Kilter Board, Tension Board, MoonBoard, and others). It is non-commercial and maintained entirely by volunteers.
intro.p2: We believe climbers should have the freedom to choose how they interact with hardware they've purchased, and that community-created data should remain accessible to the community.

facts.title: Climbs are factual data
facts.p1: A climb on a standardised board is a list of hold positions on a fixed, standardised layout (e.g. "start on A5, use B12, C3, D18, finish on K11"), combined with a grade and wall angle. This is factual, functional information — comparable to a chess position, a set of GPS coordinates, or a phone number — not a creative work of authorship.
facts.p2: Under U.S. copyright law, facts are not copyrightable (Feist Publications, Inc. v. Rural Telephone Service Co., 499 U.S. 340 (1991)). A standardised board with a finite number of holds (typically 200–500) produces climb definitions that are inherently constrained, factual, and functional.

community.title: The database is community-created
community.p1: The climb databases for these boards are almost entirely user-generated content. Individual climbers create and submit climbs. The board manufacturers did not author this content — they provide a platform for submission and display.
community.p2: The licensing position varies by manufacturer, but in no case does a manufacturer own the community's climb data:
community.aurora: Aurora Climbing (Kilter Board, Tension Board, and others): Aurora's Terms of Use grant them a "perpetual, unrestricted, unlimited, non-exclusive, irrevocable license" over user-submitted content. Crucially, this license is non-exclusive — it does not transfer ownership to Aurora, nor does it prevent the original creator (or third parties) from independently using, collecting, or presenting the same factual data.
community.moonBody: As of the last review of Moon Climbing's public-facing legal documents (February 2026), we did not find app-specific Terms of Service, an End User License Agreement, or a contributed-content license governing the MoonBoard app or its climb database. As with every board here, our position rests on the principle above: climb definitions are factual, functional data, and the databases are community-created.

compilation.title: Comprehensive databases have weak compilation protection
compilation.body: Even where a database arrangement might qualify for thin copyright protection as a compilation, the U.S. Supreme Court has held that protection extends only to creative selection or arrangement — not to the underlying facts. A database that comprehensively collects all user submissions without editorial curation (as these platforms do) is analogous to an alphabetical phone directory, which the Court found unprotectable in Feist.

attribution.title: Attribution & Respect for Creators
attribution.intro: We respect the climbing community and the people who create climbs.
attribution.item1: Where climb creator information is available, we attribute the creator by their username.
attribution.item2: We do not claim authorship of climbs we did not create.
attribution.item3Start: If you are the creator of a climb and would like it removed, please
attribution.item3End: or contact us and we will honour your request promptly.

interop.title: Interoperability & Hardware Compatibility
interop.intro: This project provides software and hardware designs that are compatible with standardised climbing board hardware. Climbers who have purchased these boards have a right to use third-party software and controllers with their own hardware.

software.title: Software interoperability
software.body: Our app communicates with board controllers over standard Bluetooth protocols. The Bluetooth communication protocol used by these boards is unencrypted and based on commodity hardware (WS2812B addressable LEDs driven by standard Bluetooth controllers). Implementing a compatible Bluetooth interface for the purpose of interoperability is well-established as lawful under both U.S. and EU law (Sega Enterprises Ltd. v. Accolade, Inc., 977 F.2d 1510 (9th Cir. 1992); EU Directive 2009/24/EC, Article 6).

controller.title: Open-source controller
controller.p1: This project also offers open-source controller hardware and firmware designs. The controller is an independent, original implementation that communicates using the same Bluetooth protocol as the official controllers. It is built on commodity components (standard microcontrollers and WS2812B LEDs) and does not incorporate any proprietary firmware, code, or hardware designs from any board manufacturer. No patents are known to exist covering the LED controller systems used by any current board manufacturer.
controller.p2: Our controller is designed to be interoperable with both this project's software and, at the user's discretion, official manufacturer apps. Any such interoperability is initiated by the end user on their own hardware.

trademark.title: Trademark Usage
trademark.body: We use board and product names (e.g. "Kilter Board", "MoonBoard", "Tension Board") solely to describe hardware compatibility and interoperability. These names are trademarks of their respective owners. This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Aurora Climbing, Moon Climbing, or any board manufacturer.

dmca.title: DMCA & Takedown Requests
dmca.intro: We take intellectual property concerns seriously. If you believe any material in this project infringes your copyright, please contact us with the following information:
dmca.item1: Identification of the copyrighted work you believe is infringed.
dmca.item2: Identification of the material you believe is infringing, with enough detail for us to locate it.
dmca.item3: Your contact information (name, address, email, phone number).
dmca.item4: A statement that you have a good faith belief that the use is not authorised by the copyright owner, its agent, or the law.
dmca.item5: A statement, under penalty of perjury, that the information in your notice is accurate and that you are the copyright owner or authorised to act on their behalf.
dmca.review1: We will review all valid requests promptly and in good faith. We may also file a counter-notice where we believe a takedown request is based on a misidentification of the material or a misunderstanding of the law.

community.title: A Note to the Community
community.p1: The climbing community has a long tradition of openly sharing beta. This project exists in that spirit. We are not trying to harm any company — we are trying to give climbers better tools to interact with hardware they already own and data they helped create.
community.p2: Manufacturers continue to benefit from this ecosystem. Our project drives demand for their physical products (holds, boards, panels) where they provide genuine value. We simply believe climbers deserve a choice in how they interact with their hardware.
community.p3: If you are a board manufacturer and would like to discuss collaboration or have concerns, we welcome open dialogue. Please reach out.

legal.footer: This document is provided for informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice. Last updated: 08-02-2026

aurora.title: Bring your Kilter or Tension logbook
aurora.intro: Link your board account once and your sends come across.
aurora.item1: Tap your avatar, then Settings, then Connected apps. Under Board Accounts, tap Link on the Tension card or Sign in to Kilter on the Kilter card, and enter that board's username and password.
aurora.item2: Used the old Kilter app? The Kilter (Aurora) card takes a JSON export instead.
aurora.item3: Sync runs one way, from their apps into Boardsesh, about every 12 hours. Nothing goes back.

climbCounts.title: Why does Kilter's app show more climbs?
climbCounts.intro: Both apps have the same climbs and count them differently.
climbCounts.item2: Kilter's app appears to count a climb once per angle it has been climbed at.
climbCounts.item3: On an 8x12 Kilter home wall that is about 18,000 climbs in Boardsesh and about 36,000 in Kilter's app.

hero.title: Make a playlist and climb it in order
hero.subtitle: Save climbs for later and load the list into your queue.

build.title: Make a playlist
build.intro: Each playlist belongs to one board.
build.step1: Open Discover. Check the board pill at the top.
build.step2: Tap the plus. Name it, pick a color, tap Create.
build.p1: To add a climb, swipe its row left, or press and hold it and tap Add to Playlist.
build.p2: The picker only shows playlists for the climb's board and layout.
build.clipAlt: Swiping a climb row left to add it to a playlist
build.clipCaption: Swipe left to file it in a playlist. Swipe right to queue it.
build.shotCaption: Pinned, then My Playlists, then For You.

remove.title: Take a climb back out
remove.p1: From the climb, open Add to Playlist and tap the ticked playlist.
remove.p2: From the playlist, tap the pencil, or choose Reorder & remove climbs from the ⋯ menu. Tap the red minus and confirm. Drag the handle to reorder.
remove.p3: For You lists have no edit mode. Un-heart a climb or log the send instead.
remove.clipCaption: Tap a ticked playlist and the climb comes back out.

queue.title: Climb the whole list
queue.intro: Tap a climb in a playlist and your queue becomes that playlist.
queue.p1: It loads in order from the climb you tapped. If climbs were queued after your current one, Start playlist? asks first. The header's play button starts from the top.
queue.p2: In a session, tapping only opens the climb for you. The shared queue stays put.
queue.sessionsLink: How a session shares one queue
queue.clipCaption: With climbs already queued, Start playlist? asks first.

smart.title: The eight lists Boardsesh builds for you
smart.crowdFavorites: Crowd Favorites. Well-rated, well-sent climbs you haven't done.
smart.hiddenGems: Hidden Gems. Rated 4.5 stars or better, sent by few.
smart.atYourLevel: At Your Level. Popular climbs around your sending grade.
smart.fresh: Fresh. New on your board, followed setters first.
smart.fiveStars: Five Stars. Climbs you rated five stars.
smart.mostRepeated: Most Repeated. Climbs with more than one logged attempt.
smart.projects: Projects. Climbs you've logged but never sent.
smart.likedClimbs: Liked Climbs. Every climb you've hearted.
smart.p1: They sit under For You on Discover. The first four read your board at your angle and skip your sends. The last four come from your ticks and hearts.
smart.p2: Tap a card's pin to move it into Pinned. Pinned For You lists stay on this phone.

tags.title: See which playlists a climb is in
tags.p1: Under Settings, then Display, turn on Show playlist tags. Rows in a playlist grow chips. Tapping a chip doesn't open the playlist.

hero.title: Live sessions with your crew
hero.subtitle: Start a session, share the link, and every phone works one queue.

start.title: Start a session
start.intro: Every session starts from the Session tab.
start.step1: Open the Session tab. Check the board at the top.
start.step2: Show this session live lets your crew see and join it. Off, only your invite link works.
start.step3: Tap Start, then Invite climbers for a QR code, Copy link and Share.
start.shotCaption: Who has joined, what's queued and what's lit.
start.liveShotCaption: Climbing now on the Home tab lists sessions you can join.

join.title: Join a session
join.way1: Scan the host's QR code or open their link.
join.way2: On the Home tab, look under Climbing now.
join.way3: Tap the board at the top of the Climbs tab, then Climbing here now.
join.p1: Each opens a Join Sam's session? card. Tap Join session.

queue.title: One queue, every phone
queue.p1: Anyone in the session can add, reorder or remove climbs. Your avatar marks your rows.
queue.p2: Only the climber who started the session can end it. Everyone else taps Leave session.

wall.title: Who lights the wall
wall.p1: A board takes one Bluetooth connection at a time. On every other phone, preview a climb and tap the lightbulb, and the connected phone lights it for you.
wall.p2: On a wall with no lights the bulb says Take the wall.

crowd.title: Browsing without moving the wall
crowd.p1: With someone else in your session, swiping stops lighting the board and a Browsing pill appears. Tap Put on the wall when you want it.
crowd.p2: Climbing alone? Hold the lightbulb and turn off Light problems on swipe and Light problems when tapping the list.
crowd.previewLink: Preview a climb from any list

history.title: Sessions on your profile
history.p1: Your profile's Sessions tab lists every session with its climbs and sends.
history.p2: The end-of-session summary has Save to Apple Health and Share to Strava. Connected apps in Settings automates it.

next.title: Keep going

hero.title: Find climbs by hold, region or setter
hero.subtitle: Where each filter on the Climbs tab lives.

start.title: Grade and angle first
start.p1: Tap the Grade pill next to search. Tap a grade to show only that grade, a second grade within three seconds for a range, and the selected grade again to clear.
start.p2: Every grade and send count is read at the board's angle. Tap the degrees chip to change it.
start.p3: Signed in, the Progress chips filter by your history. Unsent hides your sends, Projects keeps climbs tried but not sent, Not tried keeps climbs never logged.
start.clipCaption: Two quick taps build a range. Tap the same grade again to clear it.

holds.title: Filter by hold
holds.intro: Open Filters, scroll to The climb and tap Hold types.
holds.step3: Pinch to zoom, then tap holds. Tap again with the same brush to clear a mark.
holds.p2: A hold can carry more than one mark. Clear all wipes the board.
holds.clipCaption: Pick a brush first, then tap holds.

zone.title: Box off part of the wall
zone.intro: Open Filters, scroll to The climb and tap Board region.
zone.p1: Tap Add a region. Drag the middle to move the box, a corner to resize it. All holds keeps climbs entirely inside it, Any hold keeps climbs that reach in.
zone.p2: Clear region removes the box. Hold and region filters need a connection.
zone.clipCaption: Drag the middle to move the box, a corner to resize it.

setters.title: Follow setters, then search only them
setters.p1: Follow sits on a setter's page and on the Setters screen, under Filters. Then turn on Climbs by people I follow, just below Setters.
setters.p2: The Setters screen is also a picker. Check a box to filter, or tap a name to browse their climbs.
setters.shotCaption: Check a box to filter. Tap a name to browse.

rows.title: What a climb row can do
rows.p1: Swipe right to queue the climb. Swipe left for the playlist picker. Neither lights the board.
rows.p2: The small glyph is your history. A bolt means flashed, a circled tick sent, a circled cross tried, a circled C benchmark.
rows.p3: Press and hold a row for the full action menu.
rows.clipCaption: Right queues it, left opens the playlist picker.

keep.title: Keep the filters you use
keep.p1: Most filters have a pin next to their name. Tap it and the filter becomes a chip above the list.
keep.p2: The button at the bottom shows how many climbs match. Reset clears everything.

next.title: Keep going

hero.title: Log a send, then change it later
hero.subtitle: Tick a climb from the board in two taps, and change it any time.

log.title: Log it at the wall
log.p1: Tap the big tick in the play drawer, or Log ascent on the queue bar. Date and Time are filled in as now, the rest is optional.
log.p2: Attempt logs a go that didn't stick. The other button reads Flash on your first logged go at this angle, otherwise Send.
log.shotCaption: The tick opens the log sheet.
log.logbookShotCaption: Swipe right to edit, left to delete.

edit.title: Change an entry you already logged
edit.p1: Open the Profile tab, then Logbook. Swipe a row right, or press and hold it and pick Edit logbook entry.
edit.field2: Angle and Tries. Date and time stay as logged.
edit.p2: If one row bundles several goes from one day, the app asks Which entry to edit?
edit.p3: Edits need a connection. A new tick saves offline and syncs later.
edit.clipCaption: A short swipe shows the pencil or the bin. A full swipe left asks before deleting.

delete.title: Delete an entry
delete.p1: Swipe the row left, or tap Delete this ascent at the bottom of the edit sheet. Both ask to confirm. There is no undo.
delete.p2: Deleting removes the ascent's comments and votes and recounts your stats.

repeats.title: Attempts, sends and repeats
repeats.p1: One row per climb, per day, per angle. Four goes tonight are one row with tries added up and the best result showing. Mirrored goes get their own row.
repeats.p2: Next week's goes are a new row.

find.title: Find an old entry
find.p1: Search matches climb names. Filter sorts by Latest or Hardest and narrows by status, Flash only, grade, angle, date and Benchmarks only. There is no board filter.
find.p2: Sends from a linked Kilter or Tension account come across too. Tap your avatar, then Settings, then Connected apps.

next.title: Keep going
next.climbActions: Log a tick from any list

hero.title: Connect your phone to the board
hero.subtitle: Tap the lightbulb, pick your board, and your climb lights up.

connect.title: Connect
connect.p1: Tap the lightbulb in the play drawer or the top bar, then tap your board in Select Board. The list runs strongest signal first, each row with its serial.
connect.p2: The first time, iOS asks for Bluetooth. Android asks for nearby devices, or Location on Android 11 and older.
connect.litShotCaption: A filled bulb means the wall is lit.
connect.p3: At a different wall? Change board is the first row behind your avatar.

hidden.title: Hold the lightbulb
hidden.p1: While connected, press and hold the lightbulb for these controls, top to bottom.
hidden.row1: Auto-disconnect. Frees the board after 30 seconds idle. Change the time under Settings.
hidden.row2: Light the hold above. MoonBoard only.
hidden.row4: Light problems when tapping the list. Turn both off and browsing stops changing the wall.
hidden.row5: Re-light board. Sends the climb to the LEDs again.
hidden.row6: Turn off all lights. Your phone stays connected.
hidden.row7: Disconnect board. Use it when you connected to the wrong wall.
hidden.p2: A short tap reconnects to the last board you used.

failed.title: When it won't connect
failed.intro: The Couldn't connect alert names the problem.
failed.fix1: Couldn't find your board. Check it's on and you're near it. If another phone is connected, disconnect there first.
failed.fix2: Couldn't connect. Move closer and try again.
failed.fix3: Connected, but the board didn't respond. Turn the board off and on.
failed.fix4: Bluetooth is off. Turn it on.
failed.fix5: Couldn't connect to your board. Try again. If it keeps happening, turn Bluetooth off and on.
failed.p1: On Android, if nothing is found, tap Allow Location or Turn on Location at the bottom of the sheet.

twoBoards.title: Two boards in range
twoBoards.p1: Read the serial before you tap. The signal bars don't update while you stand there.
twoBoards.p2: A Board configuration doesn't match alert means the controller belongs to a different board setup. Pick Cancel, Connect anyway or Switch board setup.

duplicate.title: The same board listed twice
duplicate.p1: Two rows with different serials are two controllers. A row that reads only Kilter Board, with no serial, is a newer manufacturer-built LED box. Two of those in one gym show as two rows. The one with more signal bars is usually the wall you're standing at. If the wrong wall lights, hold the lightbulb, tap Disconnect board and try again.
duplicate.p2: There is no forget-this-device list. The app only remembers your last board.
duplicate.p3: A board showing twice under Your boards is different. Tap Edit next to Your boards, then Delete or Unfollow.

control.title: When someone else has the board
control.p1: In a session, one phone holds the board. On the others, preview a climb and tap the lightbulb, and the holder's phone lights it.
control.p2: On walls with no lights the button reads Take the wall.

liveActivity.title: Control the board from the lock screen (Live Activity)
liveActivity.intro: Start or join a session first. A solo queue doesn't get one.
liveActivity.p1: On iPhone, a session puts a Live Activity on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island with the climb, its grade and your place in the queue. While your phone holds the board it also has Previous, Next, a lightbulb that re-lights the wall, and Mirror climb where supported.
liveActivity.p2: Android shows the same controls in an ongoing notification called Active climbing session.
liveActivity.p3: Locking the screen doesn't disconnect the board.

next.title: Keep going
next.findingClimbs: Find something to put on the wall

hero.title: Press and hold a climb
hero.subtitle: Every action on a climb sits behind a long press on its row.

open.title: Open the menu
open.p1: Press and hold a climb row. It lifts into a card with Log a tick, Add to Playlist and Share on top and the rest below.
open.p2: Prefer a tap? Under Settings, then Display, turn on Show quick-actions button for a ⋮ on every Climbs row.
open.shotCaption: Three quick buttons on top, the full list below.
open.clipCaption: Hold the row and the card lifts on its own.

preview.title: Preview a climb without lighting the board
preview.intro: Preview is the first item in the list.
preview.p1: It opens the climb in the play drawer without touching your queue. Your next swipe returns to your queue.
preview.p2: In a session, or with Light problems on swipe off, a Browsing pill appears. Tap Set active or Put on the wall when you want the climb.
preview.sessionsLink: How a session keeps browsing off the wall
preview.clipCaption: The pill arrives after the swipe. The wall stays as it was.

quick.title: The three buttons across the top
quick.tick: Log a tick opens the ascent sheet.
quick.playlist: Add to Playlist is a checklist. Tick to add, untick to remove.
quick.share: Share hands a link to your phone's share sheet.
quick.p1: The card closes when an action fires, except Add to Playlist.

rest.title: The rest of the list
rest.queue: Add to queue puts the climb after your current one.
rest.favorite: Toggle favorite is the heart. Hearted climbs fill Liked Climbs.
rest.editEntry: Edit logbook entry, when you came from your logbook.
rest.betaVideo: Add beta video, when signed in.
rest.edit: Edit climb, for your own climbs as a draft or within 24 hours of publishing.
rest.remix: Remix this climb starts a new climb from these holds.
rest.openInAurora: Open in Aurora app, for Tension and other Aurora boards. Kilter has none.
rest.report: Report climb, when signed in and moderation is on.

hero.title: Attach a beta video to a climb
hero.subtitle: Boardsesh links Instagram reels and TikToks to climbs.

share.title: Share a reel from Instagram or TikTok
share.step1: On your reel or TikTok, tap Share. Pick Boardsesh. In Instagram it can hide under More.
share.step2: Boardsesh opens Attach your beta, with the post on top and your logged climbs below.
share.step3: Tap the climb the video shows. A Beta video attached message confirms it.
share.p1: There is no confirm step and no way to remove a video once attached, so check the climb name first.
share.p2: You need an account, and the climb must be in your logbook as a send or an attempt. Signed out? Sign in and the link is waiting. Only public Instagram and TikTok links work.

find.title: Find the beta on a climb
find.p1: Open a climb and scroll down to Beta Videos. Tap a card and it opens in Instagram or TikTok.
find.p2: Signed in, the plus in the section header opens Share your beta, described below.
find.p3: To list only climbs with beta, open Filters and turn on Beta videos only.

add.title: Film new beta from a climb
add.step1: Press and hold a climb and choose Add beta video, or tap the plus in its Beta Videos section.
add.step2: Tap Copy caption. It carries the climb name, angle and board.
add.step3: Tap Open Instagram and post your video with that caption.
add.step4: Share the posted reel to Boardsesh as above, or paste its link under Already have a link? and tap Attach.
add.p1: Keep the quoted climb name in the caption. It's how Boardsesh matches the reel. MoonBoard captions have no quotes, so pick the climb yourself.

shelf.title: Your beta on your profile
shelf.p1: Open the Profile tab and scroll to the bottom of Progress. The Beta videos shelf shows your latest, and See all opens the full set.
shelf.p2: Anyone can watch. A climb link shows its beta on boardsesh.com without signing in.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro1: Boardsesh is an open-source app for controlling climbing training boards (Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard) over Bluetooth. This policy explains what data we collect, why, and what we do with it.
privacy.intro2ProductAnalytics: The short version: we collect only what we need to make the app work. We do not sell your data, we do not run ads, and we do not share data with third-party marketers or data brokers.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.accountBody: When you create an account, we store your email address and username. Your email is used for authentication. Your username is displayed on your profile and visible to other users in Party Mode sessions and social features.
collect.activityBody: When you log a send or attempt, we store the climb details, grade, date, and any notes you add. This powers your logbook and progression tracking.
collect.locationBody: If you grant location permission, we use your approximate location to help you discover nearby Party Mode sessions. We do not track your location in the background or store location history.
collect.productAnalyticsBody: We use PostHog and Vercel Analytics to understand feature usage, page views, performance, and where the app is slow. Some signed-in product events are linked to your Boardsesh account so we can understand which features are useful. We do not use this data for ads.

bluetooth.title: Bluetooth
bluetooth.body: Boardsesh uses Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to connect to your climbing board's LED controller. The Bluetooth connection is used exclusively to send hold lighting commands to the board. No personal data is transmitted over Bluetooth. The app does not read data from the board beyond basic device identification during pairing.

location.title: Location data
location.body1: Location access is optional. When granted, it is used for one purpose: making your Party Mode session discoverable to nearby climbers. Your location is shared with the server only while a Party Mode session is active. We do not store your location history, build a location profile, or share location data with anyone outside of the party session discovery feature.
location.body2: You can revoke location permission at any time in your device settings. The app works fully without it.

thirdParty.title: Third-party services
thirdParty.vercelBody: We use Vercel for hosting and analytics. Vercel processes requests to serve the app and collects anonymous usage metrics. See
thirdParty.posthogBody: We use PostHog for product analytics, including server-side events for native app features like iOS Live Activities. See
thirdParty.auroraBody: If you link your Aurora Climbing account (used by Kilter and Tension boards), we sync your climb data with Aurora's servers so your logbook stays consistent across apps. This sync only happens when you initiate it. See

sharing.title: Data sharing
sharing.body1ProductAnalytics: We do not sell your data. We do not run ads. We do not share your information with third-party marketers or data brokers. The only data shared externally is what is described above (Vercel hosting/analytics, PostHog product analytics, Aurora Climbing sync when you opt in).
sharing.body2: Other Boardsesh users can see your username, profile, and logged climbs if you participate in social features like Party Mode. This is visible in the app and is part of how the product works.

retention.title: Data retention
retention.body: We keep your account data and climb history for as long as your account is active. If you stop using Boardsesh, your data stays until you delete your account.

deletion.title: Account deletion
deletion.intro: You can delete your account and all associated data at any time. There are two ways to do it:
deletion.inAppBody: Tap your avatar, open Settings, scroll to the bottom, and tap Delete Account. You will be asked to confirm before anything is removed.
deletion.onWebBodyEnd: and open Settings from your avatar menu to find the same Delete Account button.
deletion.permanent: Deletion is immediate and permanent. Once confirmed, we remove your email address, username, logbook entries, queue data, and party session history from our servers. This cannot be undone.

children.title: Children
children.body: Boardsesh is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has created an account, contact us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If we change this privacy policy, we will update this page with the new text and the "last updated" date. For significant changes, we may also notify you in the app.
